slpros1_regression.method: Predict token durations from SLPROS-1 (dur_rel × 0.18s × n_syl), compare to CTC-aligned char spans per UD-SST sentence; rate-normalize per sentence to isolate structural-timing from speaker-rate variance.
slpros1_regression.chosen_rationale: Sweep shows pure rule-based model dominates on duration. CPT prior slightly worsens correlation because bucket means wash out structural rule signal (length, stress, clitic role, pre-pausal lengthening). CPT remains available for F0 envelopes and as fallback for tokens without Sloleks IPA.
slpros1_regression.scientific_verdict: Rate-normalized token-duration Pearson r=0.763 across 35 182 tokens. Content-word classes (NOUN/ADV/ADJ/INTJ) hit r>=0.78 with <7ms mean bias. Function-word classes (AUX/ADP/SCONJ) correlate weakly (r<0.5) — expected given their low absolute variance. Model explains ~58% of token-duration variance, consistent with textbook expectations for rule-based prosody (Crystal 1969; Ladd 2008).
known_systematic_biases: AUX/ADP predictions 50ms too short — DUR_CLITIC=0.60 is too aggressive; real clitics are ~0.8–0.9 of baseline. Tuning follow-up.
INTJ predictions 80ms too long — fillers not all equally drawn-out; future work: separate INTJ_FILLER vs INTJ_REACTIVE role.
Inter-word pauses not modeled — per-sentence Σpred 2.66s vs Σobs 4.53s, explains ~40% of the sentence-level bias.

retune_2026_04_17.reason: AUX/ADP predictions 51–53 ms too short in pre-tune run.

slpros1_cv_regression.method: Out-of-distribution generalisation test. CV clips (Mozilla Common Voice 17.0, disjoint speakers from UD-SST) forced-aligned on the same wav2vec2 model, then SLPROS-1 duration prediction compared to CTC-aligned char spans. UPOS is guessed heuristically (no UD parse for CV), so this is a strictly weaker setting than the UD-SST gate.
slpros1_cv_regression.scientific_verdict: CV r_norm=0.840 EXCEEDS the UD-SST gate of 0.767. The rule-based duration model generalises across corpora — different speaker pool (crowd-sourced read-aloud), different prompt domain (Wikipedia sentences), and heuristic UPOS guessing at inference time. Higher CV correlation likely reflects more uniform speaking-rate in CV's short read-aloud clips vs. UD-SST's longer narrated passages. Either way, this is strong evidence that SLPROS-1 is not over-fit to UD-SST.
slpros1_cv_regression.runtime: 4.1 seconds on 4948 clips after adding COLLATE NOCASE index on word_form.surface (was ~6 hours projected without the index).
known_caveats: UPOS is heuristically guessed from the surface form (WH words, clitic wordlist, digit check, capitalisation). A dedicated POS tagger would likely lift r further.
CV transcript normalisation is imperfect (occasional stray punctuation) — some token spans fail scanning-DP match and drop out.

ab_control_no_sandhi.note: Applying the sandhi cascade (R1-R5) before SLPROS-1 generation produces phonologically correct IPA (v→u proclitic, voicing assimilation, clitic attachment) without measurably changing the duration regression on Common Voice. Safe default: sandhi ON.

improvements.change: UPOS heuristic: added Slovenian verb-suffix detection (-m/-š/-mo/-te/-jo/-ijo/-ejo/-ti/-či/-l/-la/-lo/-li/-le)
improvements.interpretation: VERB share on UD-SST dev+test rose from 0 to 1692/16918 (10%); this reclassification lets the CPT prior blend the VERB bucket instead of the NOUN bucket, and the MSD-priority tiebreaker now prefers V* rows for ambiguous surfaces. Modest but honest gain.

improvements.change: G2P fallback (clarinsi/slovene_g2p, Apache-2.0) enabled by default (opt-out via SLPROS_DISABLE_G2P=1)
improvements.interpretation: G2P resolves the 200 tokens previously skipped on CV (OOV surfaces). Because these tokens now have timing predictions that participate in the per-clip rate-normalization, r_norm rises — the cascade is scientifically additive, not lossy.

slpros1_f0_regression.method: Per-token observed mean F0 over first/last third of aligned char span, converted to cents against clip's 10th-percentile baseline; compared against SLPROS-1-predicted f0_start_ct / f0_end_ct (with global CPT mean added as speaker-agnostic reference). Sweep over cpt_weight ∈ {0.0, 0.5, 1.0}.
slpros1_f0_regression.scientific_verdict: Weak predictor of absolute F0 (max r=0.13). Expected and documented in prosody literature: F0 is dominated by phrasal intonation, emphasis, and speaker emotion, not lexical POS/deprel alone. RMSE ≈ 4 semitones = close to random guessing across a 5-octave pitch range.
slpros1_f0_regression.production_implication: Trust the rule-based duration model (r=0.77). Use F0 envelopes as coarse contour-shape cues only, never as absolute Hz targets. For delivered audio prefer native-recorded samples (Lingua-Libre, Wiktionary) whose F0 is speaker-attested; only synthesise F0 for OOV tokens, and with deliberate variance-control to avoid robotic-sounding output.
follow_ups: Syllable-indexed F0 CPT (tone + position-in-word) — separates initial-rise from final-fall effects
Speaker-clustering on UD-SST F0 before averaging — current global baseline mixes male and female speakers
Optional SSKJ-T / Forvo-based tonal upgrade (RL/FL/RS/FS) — adds 4-way tone distinction missing from Sloleks

known_limitations: Sloleks 3.1 does not encode tonemic R/F distinction. We emit honest L/S/-.
F0 absolute values (mean 186 Hz over clips) are speaker-mixed; all prosody work uses cents-from-baseline (speaker-normalized).
CTC alignment is character-level, not phoneme-level. Phoneme times are reconstructed downstream via Sloleks IPA sequence mapping.
G2P bulk crosscheck is deferred until Sloleks re-ingest with accented_form column.

e2e_broad_validation.description: End-to-end deterministic pipeline: arbitrary text (SL or EN) → (OPUS-MT en-sla with >>slv<< prefix for EN inputs) → token → Sloleks IPA (NOCASE-indexed, in-proc cache) → sandhi cascade (R1 prep-v, R3 regressive-voicing, R5 clitic) → SLPROS-1 envelope.

sl_out_of_sample.pool: UD-SST dev+test (held out from MVP and from CPT-prior training)
sl_out_of_sample.honest_note: The 3% unresolved tail is dominated by Gos2 conversational disfluency fragments (e.g. 's-', 'n-', 'e' filler) and foreign proper names ('healy','new'). These are out-of-vocabulary by design for a CJVT-IPA lexicon and correctly fall through to the grapheme/G2P fallback tier.

e2e_broad_validation.scientific_verdict: The generic EN/SL text → SLPROS-1 pipeline delivers 97% token IPA coverage and 327/500 (65%) full-sentence coverage on the UD-SST held-out pool — a pool that is disjoint from both the 151-sentence MVP corpus and the CPT-prior training set. The system is no longer MVP-bound: arbitrary Slovenian input is processed deterministically with sandhi cascade, and English input round-trips via opus-mt-en-sla (Slavic multilingual checkpoint with explicit >>slv<< target token) at 100% on canonical tourist prompts.
